JNJ.name: Johnson & Johnson
JNJ.numbers_line: Adjusted EPS $2.59 vs $2.52 est (beat, down 7.5% y/y on $0.64 of deal costs); revenue $25.4B vs $25.4B est, operational growth +6% (US +9.1%, outside the US +1.8%). GAAP EPS was $0.09 after ~$7B for the $5.5B talc settlement and the Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines deals.
JNJ.guidance: Raised: full-year operational sales growth 6.7–7.1% (midpoint $100.7B, the first $100B year); adjusted EPS $11.05–11.15 reported (midpoint $11.10, +2.9%, ~9% without the deal costs); operating-margin decline now ~60bp (was 75bp); tax 17–17.5%. 2027: the two deals dilute by $1.36 a share; reported growth similar to 2026 after the 53rd week; DePuy Synthes separation by mid-2027, 'leaning towards a spin'; full 2027 outlook at the 8 December enterprise review. Double-digit growth by end of decade is organic, no M&A assumed.
call_said: MedTech was the miss, +2.5% operational and 'below the standard we have set internally'. Two pockets: outside the US (China volume-based procurement, the surgery transformation) and Abiomed globally (-1.5% on a non-US high-risk PCI study the company disputes). New headwind: the Middle East conflict has spread to tender timing and spending decisions 'across a wider group of countries'. US MedTech grew almost 5%.

Innovative Medicine carried it, +7.9% with eight double-digit brands: Tremfya +68%, Rybrevant +64%, Caplyta +66%, Darzalex +15.6%. Icotyde (the oral psoriasis pill) has 20,000 patients started, 60% of them new to systemic therapy, broad commercial coverage; Inlexzo did over $90M in the quarter, ~$200M year to date, with a $5B-plus platform ambition. Oncology target: #1 by 2030 at over $50B.

Catalysts named: milvexian secondary-stroke data possibly this year, Varipulse Pro US approval in Q4, Ottava robot has its first commercial customer, four Q4 oncology readouts. Procedure volumes 'remain stable across key markets'. Free cash flow over $6B in the quarter, $21B guided; net debt ~$28B.
JNJ.quote: "Simply put, we can do better, and we absolutely will." — Tim Schmid on MedTech
JNJ.read_through: Pharma pricing and launches are intact; devices are soft outside the US and the Middle East is now a named drag on hospital tenders. Read across to ISRG (tonight) and ABT (21 Oct) for the device side, and to LLY for the oral-pill launch pattern.

UNH.name: UnitedHealth Group
UNH.numbers_line: Adjusted EPS $4.69 vs $4.14 est (large beat; $2.92 a year ago); revenue $112.7B vs $111.3B est; medical care ratio 88.4% vs 89.9% a year ago.
UNH.guidance: Full-year adjusted EPS 'at least $20.50' and called 'a solid run rate on which to grow'. For 2027 the CFO said consensus 'may understate the opportunity' and the low end of the 13–16% long-term growth rate is 'a more reasonable starting point'. Medicare Advantage margin near the top of 2–4%; Medicaid 2026 a trough at moderately better than −1%, target margins by end-2028; Optum Health pacing to 6–8% by 2028; full 2027 outlook at an investor meeting before year-end.
call_said: Commercial is the sore spot: trend above 11%, 'stabilizing' but far above history, driven by No Surprises Act arbitration (awards 10–11× Medicare, up to ~6% of medical spend in some regions), clinician intensity and specialty drugs. 2027 was priced assuming those trends persist, and the path back to high-single-digit commercial margins is 'stretched out'.

Pushed on whether cost trend is accelerating through the year (Fischbeck), Tim Noel said no: moderation in government programs, stabilisation in commercial. 2027 Medicare Advantage growth will come from D-SNP, C-SNP and high-value HMO plans, 94% footprint, prior authorisations cut 30%. Stars: nearly every HEDIS and Rx measure improved, ~75% of members in 4-star-plus plans.

AI is now an operating lever with numbers: chart summarisation for 40% of employed clinicians (review time −33%), appeal cycle times −26%, Optum Insight's Integrity One from two clients to 15 live and 24 implementing, and UNH joined the Anthropic partner network. Optum Rx is now over half external membership; specialty volumes +2.6% while total scripts fell 5%.
UNH.quote: "Current analyst consensus for 2027 may understate the opportunity ahead." — Wayne DeVeydt, CFO
UNH.read_through: Managed-care recovery is real and guided up; utilisation is high but not accelerating, which is the line that matters for ELV (21 Oct), HCA (23 or 27 Oct) and the device names. 'Demand for care remains strong' is the hospital tailwind.

DPZ.name: Domino's Pizza
DPZ.numbers_line: EPS $4.60 vs $4.36 est (beat); revenue $1.19B vs $1.17B est; US same-store sales +0.3% (carry-out +1%, delivery −0.3%), international +0.2%; operating income +8.5% ex FX.
DPZ.guidance: Cut: US comps now at the low end of low single digits; international comps about flat (Domino's Pizza Enterprises not expected to improve before 2027); US net new stores 125–150 (second cut this year), international ~800; global retail sales growth low-to-mid single digits; operating income growth mid single digits. Leverage 4.2× EBITDA and, with 'interest rates accelerating pretty significantly', the company may run below the 4× floor of its range.
call_said: New CEO Joe Jordan (Russell Weiner to executive chairman in April) and a new product, the Domino, pulled forward because of the ticket problem and the aggregator opportunity. Priorities: closer to the customer, franchisee four-wall profit, 'turn our best performance into our everyday performance'.

The consumer in one metric: order counts grew again, including among low-income customers, but items per order fell in both carry-out and first-party delivery as customers 'managed their ticket'. The macro overhang is expected to last through the year; franchisee profits are down in dollars, which is what is slowing store openings. GLP-1 pill: 'no meaningful impact with what we know today', still studying.

Third-party delivery: #1 in pizza on both DoorDash and Uber, about 50% incremental, not yet at fair share. Supply-chain margin beat on productivity and route optimisation; profit shared 50/50 with franchisees. Jordan is 'more encouraged on DPE than in quite some time' after meeting its new CEO.
DPZ.quote: "Consumers remain under pressure, but they continue to choose Domino's." — Joe Jordan
DPZ.read_through: The clearest consumer tell of the week: traffic up, basket down, value promotions everywhere, and the cost of debt now shaping capital allocation at a 4× levered franchisor. Read across to MCD, KO (27 Oct) and the rest of the consumer tape.

ASML.name: ASML
ASML.numbers_line: FMP: EPS $14.47 vs $12.18 est (beat), revenue $12.97B vs $13.14B est. In euros: record sales €11.7B at the high end of guidance, gross margin 57.5%, EPS €12.95 including ~€500M of Mistral AI revaluation; installed-base sales €3.3B, €400M above guidance.
ASML.guidance: Q4 sales €14.2–15.2B at ~57% gross margin; full year €44–45B (+36%) at ~56%: EUV +45%, non-EUV systems +20%, installed base +50%; memory +75%, logic +10% (advanced logic +25%); China ~20%. Capacity: ~65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026 (+50%), +30% in 2027 for EUV and immersion, and 2028 now planned above +30%. Price increases on the most critical products agreed: some effect in 2027, the full effect from 2028. Next-gen NXE:3800F (260 wph) in small volume early 2027; immersion to 330 wph.
call_said: Customers 'have concluded that demand for their product will outpace supply through at least 2028' and are accelerating fabs; orders for 2028 are arriving and customers are asking to place 2029 and 2030 orders, which ASML is holding until it can allocate fairly. Down payments 'enough to hurt' are in the €5B jump in non-current liabilities; free cash flow €11.4B.

The price rise was 'one of the very first times' ASML has had that conversation, accepted by customers, not to be repeated every year, backlog not repriced. Gross margin dips in Q4 on ramp costs; the upgrade business (€400M beat) is the swing factor for 2027 margin.

High-NA is moving to production: Intel has exposed over a million wafers, Samsung 2028 and TSMC 2030 for high volume, a 12-inch mask consortium led by TSMC. New DRAM customers are adopting EUV 'beyond the T customer'. Zeiss and the supply chain are not the bottleneck; customer clean rooms are not either. China demand 'intrinsically strong' into 2027.
ASML.quote: "Demand for their product will outpace supply through at least 2028." — Christophe Fouquet, on what customers are telling ASML
ASML.read_through: This is the chip pack's demand signal in one number: memory tool sales up 75% this year, mostly DRAM. Bullish for MU, SNDK, WDC on the cycle, for LRCX (21 Oct), AMAT and KLAC on capex, and it says TSM's capex is going up, not down.

BAC.name: Bank of America
BAC.numbers_line: EPS $1.08 vs $1.10 est (adjusted for the $1.2B settlement; reported $0.91); revenue $30.0B vs $30.6B est; NII $16.6B +8%, net interest yield 2.16%. The stock opened down ~8% and analysts said so on the call.
BAC.guidance: NII up sequentially in Q4 and through 2027; full-year 2026 NII growth ~8%; 2027 NII growth '8% or more' assuming three 25bp hikes (December, March, June); back to positive operating leverage in Q4 and 200–300bp medium term; buybacks 'business as usual' pending the final capital rules; GSIB surcharge step-up takes the minimum to 10.5% in January.
call_said: The $1.2B OCC/FinCEN anti-money-laundering settlement (from the December 2024 consent order) is non-deductible, carries no asset cap, and the thousands of staff and the technology are 'in the run rate'; two analysts called it a 'confidence issue' given management had said the cost was already absorbed in January 2025.

FICC −17%: rates rose 85bp in the quarter and BAC's mix (credit, mortgages, municipals) is what gets hurt when that happens; equities a record third quarter, +10%. 'When customers stop cold like they did last quarter, that happens.' Fourth-quarter markets may not see the usual seasonal drop. Balance sheet shrank 2% as wholesale funding was run off.

Consumer and credit: spend +5% with gas up 20-odd percent crowding out a little, paychecks growing across all three income bands, card loss rate 3.22% and falling, commercial criticised assets at the lowest since 4Q19, CRE office at the 'very tail end'. AI: 130 projects, benefits ~$300M this year to ~$700M next, headcount down 3,500; on AI agents moving deposits, 'the human remains in the loop'.
BAC.quote: "I know we're all desperate for the final rules. I'm desperate for the final rules." — Alastair Borthwick, CFO
BAC.read_through: The credit book at the largest consumer bank is the cleanest since 2019; the sell-off was the fine plus a FICC mix problem, not the consumer. Three more hikes by June 2027 are now written into bank guidance, which is the rate backdrop every rate-sensitive name in the universe is trading on.
